verdicts.title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them — every displayed time silently stays on the host's timezone
verdicts.location_wrong: The cited root cause only half explains the symptom. clock_provider.dart:219 _parseTimezoneOffset does reject the 17 IANA names (verified in source), but 'UTC' — the one entry it DOES parse (Duration.zero) — changes nothing either: with timezone=UTC and use_system_time=false the status-bar clock still read 12:04:44 host EDT instead of 16:04 UTC. The real cause for the surfaces cited as evidence is that they never consult clockProvider at all: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/widgets/status_bar.dart:188/200/209 uses raw DateTime.now(), and only 6 call sites app-wide read clockProvider (session_detail_dialog, session_provider, scheduler_provider, imaging_service). A fixer who only widened the parser per the finding's 'where' would leave the status bar and dashboard exactly as broken.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced on display :85, fresh profile. Set site to Seattle (47.6062/-122.3321/1234 m), then Settings > Location > Time. (1) use_system_time OFF with timezone=UTC: DB shows use_system_time|false, timezone|UTC; status-bar clock 12:04:44 while `date -u` = 16:04:44 — unchanged host-local. (2) Set Timezone = Asia/Tokyo (DB: timezone|Asia/Tokyo, use_system_time|false): status bar still 12:05:48 while `TZ=Asia/Tokyo date` = 01:05:48. (3) Dashboard Moon card byte-identical across both timezones (Moonrise 00:55 / Moonset 13:24), and the header clock chip likewise host-local. So the picker is inert on every surface I could reach. Severity: the control is dead and the app displays a timezone it does not honour, but nothing it computes is wrong-by-timezone (LST/twilight are longitude-driven, capture timestamps stay host-local and self-consistent), so this is a dead-setting/false-claim defect rather than a night-costing one — P2.

verdicts.title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place — producing a site that does not exist
verdicts.location_wrong: location_settings.dart:240-285 is right (the row, and `elevation: settings.elevation` passed unchanged, are there). geolocation_service.dart:7-14 is wrong: lines 7-14 are the doc comment + signature of fetchLocationFromIP. fetchLocationFromGPS is at :108-193 and is NOT 'not GPS at all' — it calls Geolocator.isLocationServiceEnabled/checkPermission/getCurrentPosition first and only falls back to IP (fetchLocation at :98-106) when that fails, which it always does on Linux desktop. A fixer told 'this function just GETs ipapi.co' would delete the wrong code. Also note the observed request was NOT ipapi.co: ipapi.co is currently rate-limited from this host (curl returns {"error":true,"reason":"RateLimited"}), so the app used the second fallback fetchLocationFromIPAlternative at :52-95, which is plain-HTTP http://ip-api.com/json/ — a cleartext outbound request, worse than the HTTPS one the finding describes.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. Set the site to Seattle 47.6062 / -122.3321 with elevation 1234 m (confirmed in app_settings and in the Rust log: 'Setting observer location: lat=47.6062, lon=-122.3321, elev=1234'). Clicked the crosshair on 'Use Device Location / Get location from GPS'. sqlite3 immediately after: observer_latitude|39.9817, observer_longitude|-75.4072, observer_elevation|1234.0 — coordinates replaced by an IP lookup, elevation left at the Seattle value. Independently confirmed the source of those numbers: `curl http://ip-api.com/json/` from this host returns lat 39.9817, lon -75.4072, city Newtown Square, region Pennsylvania — an exact match, so this is IP geolocation over a third-party service, as claimed. The resulting site (Newtown Square PA at 1234 m; PA's highest point is 979 m) is indeed impossible. Severity corrected to P2: the mislabel and the undisclosed third-party call are real honesty/privacy defects and the stale elevation is a real correctness bug, but elevation only perturbs refraction/horizon at the arcsecond level and the user still gets roughly the right coordinates, so it neither costs a night nor endangers gear.

verdicts.title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' for an address nothing can connect to
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced twice, on my own display/profile. (a) Host 192.0.2.1 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1) port 7624: the dialog showed 'Testing...' for ~30 s and then a green check with 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' — /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/13-dlg-crop.png shows the host field reading 192.0.2.1 next to that message. From the same host `timeout 6 bash -c 'echo > /dev/tcp/192.0.2.1/7624'` exits 124 (hangs, never connects). (b) Host 127.0.0.1 port 9, where the OS refuses instantly (`/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9` -> 'Connection refused'): identical green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' — /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/15-dlg-after.png shows host 127.0.0.1, port 9, and the green message together. Nothing appeared in the app log for either attempt. Cause verified as cited AND one level deeper: the Rust side is honest — native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/discovery.rs:153-168 api_discover_indi_at_address map_err's the failure into SkotiqError::connection_failed — and it is the Dart wrapper _discoverAddressDevices (discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102) that catches it and returns `const <DeviceInfo>[]`, so indi_server_dialog.dart's catch at :131 is unreachable and :129 always renders the success string. Both cited locations are correct. P1 stands: the button exists solely to answer 'is this address reachable before dark', and it answers 'yes' unconditionally.

verdicts.title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore says 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' — same app, same second, same fact
verdicts.duplicate_of: Shares one root cause with 'Auto-Save & Backups renders compiled-in defaults instead of the saved settings' — both are the Settings page reading an AutoSaveService instance that nothing ever hydrated. Fixing that provider wiring fixes both; they are worth keeping as separate findings only because the user-visible symptoms differ (false 'Never' vs. silently reverted config).
verdicts.location_wrong: auto_save_service.dart:149-166 is NOT where the bug is. That block is correct and even carries a comment describing this exact symptom, and it publishes the hydrated status (_statusController.add(_status)). What I found is that the hydration never reaches the instance the page sees: autoSaveServiceProvider (auto_save_service.dart:690) `ref.watch(backendProvider)`, so the service is rebuilt when the backend swaps, while autoSaveLifecycleProvider — the only caller of start(config, lastBackup) — is read exactly once, unawaited, at apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:280 and is not watched by anything afterwards. Note also start() begins with `if (_started) return;`, so a service that was started without arguments can never be hydrated later. The fix site is the provider wiring / the page's ref.watch at auto_save_settings.dart:179, not the start() body.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced both halves on my own profile. (1) SAME-SESSION CONTRADICTION: with app_settings holding autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-02T16:03:47.621627Z (= 12:03 local, written by this app process), Settings > GENERAL > Files & Storage > Status read 'Last backup / Never' with trailing 'Pending' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/23-files2.png), while Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore, read minutes later in the same session, showed 'Auto-Save Status / Last Sequence Save Never / Last Full Backup Aug 2, 2026 12:03' plus a Recent Backups list with real .nsbackup files. (2) Pressing 'Back Up Now' corrected the card to '0s ago' / 'In 23h' and the key became 2026-08-02T16:15:01.581767Z. (3) STRONGER REPRO HELD: after `stop` + `start` on the same profile (pid 2285313), with autosave.last_backup_at still = 16:15:01.581767Z in the DB, Files & Storage again renders 'Last backup / Never / Pending' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/24-post-restart.png). So the persisted timestamp is never hydrated into this card. P1 stands: a false 'Never' about data protection is exactly the cry-wolf class — it invites either a panic or a shrug, and one of the two surfaces is lying at all times.

verdicts.title: Auto-Save & Backups renders compiled-in defaults instead of the saved settings, and changing any one field silently overwrites the other four
verdicts.duplicate_of: Same root as the 'Last backup: Never' finding (unhydrated AutoSaveService instance); the clobber half is additional and is not covered by that one.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly as written. Before restart I set 'Enable sequence auto-save' ON and 'Maximum backups' 50; sqlite3 confirmed autosave.sequence_enabled|true, autosave.max_backups|50, autosave.backup_interval_hours|24. Stopped and relaunched the same profile. The page then rendered the compiled-in defaults — switch OFF, Maximum backups 7, Backup interval 24, Last backup Never (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/24-post-restart.png) — while the DB still held sequence_enabled|true and max_backups|50. I then changed ONLY 'Backup interval' 24 -> 12. sqlite3 immediately after: autosave.backup_interval_hours|12 (correct) and autosave.sequence_enabled|false, autosave.max_backups|7 — one edit destroyed two persisted settings, including turning sequence auto-save off. The cited mechanism checks out: auto_save_settings.dart:179 does `ref.watch(autoSaveServiceProvider)` (raw service, defaults) and _updateConfig at :68-84 does service.config.copyWith(...) then _persistAutoSaveConfig (auto_save_service.dart:854-861) rewrites all five autosave.* keys from that stale object. The finding's 'where' says lines 178-180; the watch is on 179 — close enough to act on. P1 stands: silently disabling a data-protection feature the user explicitly enabled is a data-loss-adjacent defect, not cosmetic.

verdicts.title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently — every screen gets an undismissable red 'Error: not connected to server' banner and there is no way back without a restart
verdicts.location_wrong: app_shell.dart:653-671 is exactly right (the `if (!useBottomNav && ref.watch(sequencerBackendProvider) is DisconnectedBackend)` banner). The second half of the 'where' — connection_settings.dart — is only the dialog that calls `ref.read(backendProvider.notifier).connect(...)` at :472; it does not choose the post-failure state. The decision a fixer must change lives in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/backend_provider.dart:194-228 `_rollbackFailedConnect`, which deliberately installs a FRESH DisconnectedBackend on a failed connect rather than restoring the previously-installed local FfiBackend. `useLocalBackend()` (backend_provider.dart:249-259, the only site that constructs FfiBackend) has no UI caller at all, which is why there is no way back short of relaunch.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced on a desktop profile with nothing listening on 8080 (`ss -ltn` shows no :8080 listener). Before: Settings > Connection read 'Server Status / Local' and 'Connection Status / Local Mode'. Opened Connect to Server, left localhost:8080, pressed Connect: the dialog correctly reported 'Connection failed: Connection to http://localhost:8080 did not complete (state=disconnected).' After dismissing it the page reads 'Server Status / Not connected' and 'Connection Status / Disconnected', and a full-width red 'Error: not connected to server' bar is pinned under the title bar — verified on Dashboard (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/27-dash-banner.png) and Equipment (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsg/28-equip.png), with no close affordance. The title-bar connection popover shows only 'Connection Status / Not connected to a server' with no buttons, and an accessibility-tree dump of the whole Connection page lists exactly two buttons — 'Configure' and 'Connect' — so nothing offers 'continue locally'. Extra contradiction the finding did not note: the Dashboard header chip still says 'Local' while the banner two rows above says the app is not connected to a server. P1 stands: on the machine that owns the hardware, one mistyped host permanently replaces the local backend (all role providers watch backendProvider) and leaves a standing red error on a rig that is otherwise fine — the cry-wolf pattern this project has already been bitten by.
